items.name: Strength Building
items.text: Progressive resistance training increases muscle strength and power output over time.

items.name: Muscle Growth
items.text: Mechanical tension and metabolic stress from training stimulate muscle hypertrophy.

items.name: Bone Density
items.text: Weight-bearing exercises increase bone mineral density and reduce osteoporosis risk.

items.name: Metabolic Health
items.text: Regular training improves insulin sensitivity and glucose metabolism.

items.name: Cardiovascular Health
items.text: Exercise strengthens the heart and improves circulation throughout the body.

items.name: Mental Health
items.text: Physical activity reduces stress, anxiety, and improves overall mood.

items.name: Joint Health
items.text: Proper exercise strengthens connective tissue and improves joint stability.

items.name: Posture Improvement
items.text: Balanced training corrects muscular imbalances and improves body alignment.

items.name: Progressive Overload
items.text: Gradually increase weight, reps, or volume over time to continue making progress.

items.name: Specificity
items.text: Training adaptations are specific to the type of stimulus applied.

items.name: Variation
items.text: Periodically change exercises, intensity, or volume to prevent plateaus.

items.name: Recovery
items.text: Adequate rest between sessions allows for muscle repair and growth.

items.name: Individualization
items.text: Programs should be tailored to individual goals, experience, and recovery capacity.

items.name: Consistency
items.text: Regular training over time is more important than perfect individual sessions.

items.name: Mind-Muscle Connection
items.text: Focus on feeling the target muscle work during each repetition.

items.name: Full Range of Motion
items.text: Use complete ROM for maximum muscle activation and joint health.

items.name: Proper Warm-Up
items.text: Begin with 5-10 minutes of light cardio and dynamic stretching before training.

items.name: Form Before Weight
items.text: Master proper technique with lighter loads before increasing resistance.

items.name: Breathing Technique
items.text: Exhale during exertion, inhale during the easier phase of the movement.

items.name: Listen to Your Body
items.text: Distinguish between productive discomfort and pain that signals injury.

items.name: Use a Spotter
items.text: Have assistance for heavy compound lifts, especially near failure.

items.name: Equipment Check
items.text: Inspect equipment before use and ensure proper setup and adjustments.

items.name: Stay Hydrated
items.text: Drink water before, during, and after training to maintain performance.

items.name: Cool Down
items.text: End sessions with light activity and static stretching to aid recovery.

items.name: Protein Intake
items.text: Consume 1.6-2.2g of protein per kg of bodyweight daily for muscle growth.

items.name: Pre-Workout Nutrition
items.text: Eat a balanced meal 2-3 hours before training for optimal energy.

items.name: Post-Workout Recovery
items.text: Consume protein and carbohydrates within 2 hours after training.

items.name: Carbohydrate Timing
items.text: Focus carb intake around training sessions to fuel performance and recovery.

items.name: Healthy Fats
items.text: Include sources like nuts, avocados, and fish for hormone production.

items.name: Micronutrients
items.text: Eat a variety of fruits and vegetables for vitamins and minerals.

items.name: Meal Frequency
items.text: Distribute protein intake across 3-5 meals throughout the day.

items.name: Sleep and Recovery
items.text: Aim for 7-9 hours of quality sleep nightly for optimal muscle recovery.
